Consider the CO2 molecule. It has 16 valence electrons (4 from the carbon and 6 from each oxygen). Two electrons on each oxygen atom are nonbonding elec- trons in 2s atomic orbitals. Of the remaining 12 electrons, 4 take part in localized s bonds, 2 between each oxygen and the carbon. This leaves 8 electrons for the p system. Placing them in the correlation diagram of Figure 6.41 gives two electron pairs in p orbitals and two pairs in pnb orbitals. The total bond order for the mol- ecule is 4, because there are two pairs of electrons in p bonding orbitals (from the sp hybrids) and two pairs in p bonding orbitals (the nonbonding pnb and atomic oxygen 2s orbitals neither increase nor decrease the bond order). Each bond is then of order 2, in agreement with the Lewis diagram result for CO2. The meaning is slightly different here, however, in that some of the bonding electrons (those in the p orbital system) are delocalized over the full molecule rather than shared by only two of the atoms.

If the molecule lies in the x-y plane, then the s, px, and py orbitals of the central atom can be combined to form three sp2 hybrid orbitals with an angle close to 120° between each pair. One of these orbitals holds a lone pair of electrons, and the other two take part in s bonds with the outer atoms. The fourth orbital, a pz orbital, takes part in delocal- ized p bonding (Fig. 6.42a). On the outer atoms, the p orbital pointing toward the central atom takes part in a localized s bond, and the pz orbital takes part in p bonding; the third p orbital and the s orbital are AOs that do not participate in bonding. The three pz AOs can be combined into bonding, nonbonding, and antibonding p orbitals much as in the linear molecule case (Fig. 6.42a). Here there is only one of each type of orbital (p, pnb, p*) rather than two as for linear molecules.

Two electrons also are placed as a lone pair in the third sp2 orbital of the nitrogen atom. Of the remaining 8 electrons, 4 are involved in the two s bonds between nitrogen and the oxygen atoms. The last 4 are placed into the p electron system: 2 into the bonding p orbital and 2 into the nonbonding pnb orbital. Because a total of 6 electrons are in bonding orbitals and none are in antibonding, the net bond order for the molecule is 3, or 1 1 2 per bond.
